children: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX, Financials) may be about to get a large new buyer. Not because its business changed. Because its index weight might.
J.P. Morgan strategists estimate SpaceX could attract roughly $15.5 billion of net buying from passive funds if its Nasdaq-100 weighting rises at the next quarterly rebalance.
SpaceX currently represents about 1.25% of the index even though its market value exceeds $2 trillion. The gap comes from its relatively small public float.

Nasdaq limits the index weight of companies with fewer shares available for public trading. But more than 1 billion SpaceX shares have now been released from post-IPO restrictions, lifting the free float to nearly 30% from less than 10%.

That could push SpaceX's weighting to about 2.25%, according to J.P. Morgan. Funds tracking the Nasdaq-100 would then need to buy more shares simply to match the index. The changes are scheduled to be announced Friday and take effect Sept. 21. There is another side to the story.
More than 1 billion additional shares are expected to become eligible for sale by the end of October, followed by another 1.3 billion after third-quarter results in November.
That creates an unusual tug of war. Passive funds could be forced to buy billions of dollars of stock at the same time insiders gain the ability to sell much more of it.
Earlier August lockup expirations did not produce the sharp selloff some investors expected. The larger releases ahead could be a tougher test.
The next catalyst is Friday's Nasdaq-100 rebalance announcement, which should show whether SpaceX is about to receive a major wave of index-driven demand.

title: SpaceX Could Be Heading for a $15.5 Billion Index Boost
